sanskrit: karṇajaṅghaś ca bhagavān gālavaś ca mahān ṛṣiḥ ṛṣir vajras tathākhyātaḥ śālaṅkāyana eva ca
english: There was the venerable Karṇajaṅgha, and Gālava the great sage, the seer renowned as Vajra, and Śālaṅkāyana too.

sanskrit: lālāṭyo nāradaś caiva tathā kūrcamukhaḥ smṛtaḥ vādulir musalaś caiva rakṣogrīvas tathaiva ca
english: Lālāṭya and Nārada, and likewise Kūrcamukha as he is remembered, Vāduli and Musala, and Rakṣogrīva as well.

sanskrit: aṅghriko naikabhṛc caiva śilāyūpaḥ sitaḥ śuciḥ cakrako mārutantavyo vātaghno 'thāśvalāyanaḥ
english: Aṅghrika and Naikabhṛt, Śilāyūpa, Sītā, Śuci, Cakraka, Mārutantavya, Vātaghna, and then Aśvalāyana.

sanskrit: śyāmāyano 'tha gārgyaś ca jābāliḥ suśrutas tathā kārīṣir atha saṃśrutyaḥ parapauravatantavaḥ
english: Śyāmāyana, and Gārgya, Jābāli, and Suśruta likewise, then Kārīṣi and Saṃśrutya, and the Parapauravatantavas.

sanskrit: mahān ṛṣiś ca kapilas tatharṣis tārakāyanaḥ tathaiva copagahanas tatharṣiś cārjunāyanaḥ
english: The great sage Kapila, and the seer Tārakāyana, and likewise Upagahana, and the seer Arjunāyana.

sanskrit: mārgamitrir hiraṇyākṣo jaṅghārir babhruvāhanaḥ sūtir vibhūtiḥ sūtaś ca suraṅgaś ca tathaiva hi
english: Mārgamitri, Hiraṇyākṣa, Jaṅghāri, Babhruvāhana, Sūti, Vibhūti, and Sūta, and Suraṅga too, indeed.

sanskrit: ārāddhir nāmayaś caiva cāmpeyojjayanau tathā navatantur bakanakhaḥ śayonaratir eva ca
english: Ārāddhi and Nāmaya, and Cāmpeya and Ujjayana likewise, Navatantu, Bakanakha, and Śayonarati as well.

sanskrit: śayoruhaś cārumatsyaḥ śirīṣī cātha gārdabhiḥ ujjayonir adāpekṣī nāradī ca mahān ṛṣiḥ viśvāmitrātmajāḥ sarve munayo brahmavādinaḥ
english: Śayoruha, Cārumatsya, Śirīṣī, and then Gārdabhi, Ujjayoni, Adāpekṣī, and Nāradī the great sage — all these are the sons of Viśvāmitra, sages and expounders of the Veda.

sanskrit: tan naiṣa kṣatriyo rājan viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ ṛcīkenāhitaṃ brahma param etad yudhiṣṭhira
english: Therefore, O king, this Viśvāmitra of mighty austerities is no kṣatriya; this supreme brahminhood was implanted in him by Ṛcīka, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ tattvena bharatarṣabha viśvāmitrasya vai janma somasūryāgnitejasaḥ
english: All this I have told you in truth, O bull of the Bharatas — the birth of Viśvāmitra, whose splendor was that of Soma, Sūrya, and Agni.

sanskrit: yatra yatra ca saṃdeho bhūyas te rājasattama tatra tatra ca māṃ brūhi cchettāsmi tava saṃśayān
english: And wherever a doubt may yet arise in you, O best of kings, there ask of me, and I shall sever your uncertainties.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ānṛśaṃsasya dharmasya guṇān bhaktajanasya ca śrotum icchāmi kārtsnyena tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I wish to hear in full the virtues of the dharma of compassion and of the devoted person; tell me that, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca viṣaye kāśirājasya grāmān niṣkramya lubdhakaḥ saviṣaṃ kāṇḍam ādāya mṛgayām āsa vai mṛgam
english: Bhīṣma said: In the realm of the king of Kāśi, a hunter, having set out from the villages and taken a poisoned arrow, went hunting for game.

sanskrit: tatra cāmiṣalubdhena lubdhakena mahāvane avidūre mṛgaṃ dṛṣṭvā bāṇaḥ pratisamāhitaḥ
english: There in the great forest, the hunter, greedy for meat, having seen a deer not far off, fitted his arrow to the bow.

sanskrit: tena durvāritāstreṇa nimittacapaleṣuṇā mahān vanatarur viddho mṛgaṃ tatra jighāṃsatā
english: By that man of irresistible weapon, whose shaft swerved from its mark, a great forest tree was struck as he sought to slay the deer there.

sanskrit: sa tīkṣṇaviṣadigdhena śareṇātibalātkṛtaḥ utsṛjya phalapatrāṇi pādapaḥ śoṣam āgataḥ
english: That tree, overborne by the arrow smeared with keen poison, shed its fruits and leaves and withered away.

sanskrit: tasmin vṛkṣe tathābhūte koṭareṣu ciroṣitaḥ na jahāti śuko vāsaṃ tasya bhaktyā vanaspateḥ
english: In that tree, brought to such a state, a parrot long dwelling in its hollows did not abandon his abode, out of devotion to that lord of the forest.

sanskrit: niṣpracāro nirāhāro glānaḥ śithilavāg api kṛtajñaḥ saha vṛkṣeṇa dharmātmā sa vyaśuṣyata
english: Going nowhere, taking no food, weary, his voice grown faint, that grateful and righteous bird withered away together with the tree.

sanskrit: tam udāraṃ mahāsattvam atimānuṣaceṣṭitam samaduḥkhasukhaṃ jñātvā vismitaḥ pākaśāsanaḥ
english: Learning of that noble bird of great spirit, whose conduct surpassed the human and who shared alike in joy and sorrow with the tree, the Chastiser of Pāka was amazed.

sanskrit: tataś cintām upagataḥ śakraḥ katham ayaṃ dvijaḥ tiryagyonāv asaṃbhāvyam ānṛśaṃsyaṃ samāsthitaḥ
english: Then Śakra fell to pondering: How is it that this bird, born in the brute creation, has taken his stand on a compassion scarcely to be conceived of there?

sanskrit: atha vā nātra citraṃ hīty abhavad vāsavasya tu prāṇinām iha sarveṣāṃ sarvaṃ sarvatra dṛśyate
english: Yet, thought Vāsava, there is nothing strange in this; for among all living beings here, everything may be seen everywhere.

sanskrit: tato brāhmaṇaveṣeṇa mānuṣaṃ rūpam āsthitaḥ avatīrya mahīṃ śakras taṃ pakṣiṇam uvāca ha
english: Then Śakra, having assumed a human form in the guise of a brāhmaṇa, descended to the earth and spoke to that bird.

sanskrit: śuka bhoḥ pakṣiṇāṃ śreṣṭha dākṣeyī suprajās tvayā pṛcche tvā śuṣkam etaṃ vai kasmān na tyajasi drumam
english: O parrot, best of birds, the daughter of Dakṣa has been blessed with worthy offspring through you; I ask you — why do you not forsake this withered tree?

sanskrit: atha pṛṣṭaḥ śukaḥ prāha mūrdhnā samabhivādya tam svāgataṃ devarājāya vijñātas tapasā mayā
english: Thus questioned, the parrot, bowing to him with his head, replied: Welcome to the king of the gods, whom I have recognized through my austerity.

sanskrit: tato daśaśatākṣeṇa sādhu sādhv iti bhāṣitam aho vijñānam ity evaṃ tapasā pūjitas tataḥ
english: Then by the Thousand-eyed one it was said, "Well done, well done! Ah, what discernment!" — and thus was the bird honored for his austerity.

sanskrit: tam evaṃ śubhakarmāṇaṃ śukaṃ paramadhārmikam vijānann api tāṃ prāptiṃ papraccha balasūdanaḥ
english: Though he well knew the bird's attainment, the Slayer of Bala questioned that parrot of holy deeds and supreme righteousness.

sanskrit: niṣpatram aphalaṃ śuṣkam aśaraṇyaṃ patatriṇām kimarthaṃ sevase vṛkṣaṃ yadā mahad idaṃ vanam
english: "Leafless, fruitless, withered, no refuge for birds — why do you cling to this tree, when this forest is so vast?

sanskrit: anye 'pi bahavo vṛkṣāḥ patrasaṃchannakoṭarāḥ śubhāḥ paryāptasaṃcārā vidyante 'smin mahāvane
english: Many other trees, their hollows shaded with leaves, fair and offering ample range, are to be found in this great forest.

sanskrit: gatāyuṣam asāmarthyaṃ kṣīṇasāraṃ hataśriyam vimṛśya prajñayā dhīra jahīmaṃ hy asthiraṃ drumam
english: Reflect with wisdom, O steadfast one: this tree's life is spent, its strength is gone, its sap is drained, its splendor destroyed — forsake this perishing tree."

sanskrit: tad upaśrutya dharmātmā śukaḥ śakreṇa bhāṣitam sudīrgham abhiniḥśvasya dīno vākyam uvāca ha
english: Hearing this spoken by Śakra, the righteous parrot, sighing long and deeply, in distress uttered these words:

sanskrit: anatikramaṇīyāni daivatāni śacīpate yatrābhavas tatra bhavas tan nibodha surādhipa
english: "The decrees of the gods are not to be transgressed, O lord of Śacī; where one came to be, there one abides — understand this, O sovereign of the gods.

sanskrit: asminn ahaṃ drume jātaḥ sādhubhiś ca guṇair yutaḥ bālabhāve ca saṃguptaḥ śatrubhiś ca na dharṣitaḥ
english: In this tree I was born, and endowed with good qualities; in my infancy I was sheltered here and never assailed by enemies.

sanskrit: kim anukrośavaiphalyam utpādayasi me 'nagha ānṛśaṃsye 'nuraktasya bhaktasyānugatasya ca
english: Why, O sinless one, do you make my compassion come to nothing — mine, who am devoted to kindness, attached and faithful to this tree?

sanskrit: anukrośo hi sādhūnāṃ sumahad dharmalakṣaṇam anukrośaś ca sādhūnāṃ sadā prītiṃ prayacchati
english: For compassion is the great mark of the dharma of the good, and the compassion of the good ever bestows delight.

sanskrit: tvam eva daivataiḥ sarvaiḥ pṛcchyase dharmasaṃśayān atas tvaṃ deva devānām ādhipatye pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: You yourself are asked by all the gods to resolve their doubts about dharma; therefore, O god, you stand established in sovereignty over the gods.

sanskrit: nārhasi tvaṃ sahasrākṣa tyājayitveha bhaktitaḥ samartham upajīvyemaṃ tyajeyaṃ katham adya vai
english: You ought not, O Thousand-eyed one, to make me abandon this out of my devotion; how should I now forsake this tree on which I have lived and which once sustained me?"

sanskrit: tasya vākyena saumyena harṣitaḥ pākaśāsanaḥ śukaṃ provāca dharmajñam ānṛśaṃsyena toṣitaḥ
english: Gladdened by his gentle words and pleased by his compassion, the Chastiser of Pāka spoke to that parrot who knew dharma:

sanskrit: varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti tadā sa ca vavre varaṃ śukaḥ ānṛśaṃsyaparo nityaṃ tasya vṛkṣasya saṃbhavam
english: "Choose a boon!" — and then the parrot, ever devoted to compassion, chose as his boon the restoration of that tree.

sanskrit: viditvā ca dṛḍhāṃ śakras tāṃ śuke śīlasaṃpadam prītaḥ kṣipram atho vṛkṣam amṛtenāvasiktavān
english: And Śakra, knowing that firm wealth of character in the parrot, was pleased, and at once sprinkled the tree with the nectar of immortality.

sanskrit: tataḥ phalāni patrāṇi śākhāś cāpi manoramāḥ śukasya dṛḍhabhaktitvāc chrīmattvaṃ cāpa sa drumaḥ
english: Then, through the parrot's steadfast devotion, that tree regained its fruits, its leaves, its lovely branches, and its splendor.

sanskrit: śukaś ca karmaṇā tena ānṛśaṃsyakṛtena ha āyuṣo 'nte mahārāja prāpa śakrasalokatām
english: And the parrot, by that deed wrought of compassion, O great king, at the end of his life attained to the same world as Śakra.

sanskrit: evam eva manuṣyendra bhaktimantaṃ samāśritaḥ sarvārthasiddhiṃ labhate śukaṃ prāpya yathā drumaḥ
english: Even so, O lord of men, one who takes refuge with a devoted being attains the fulfillment of all his aims, as the tree did by gaining the parrot.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaha mahāprājña sarvaśāstraviśārada daive puruṣakāre ca kiṃ svic chreṣṭhataraṃ bhavet
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O grandfather, greatly wise, versed in all the scriptures — between fate and human effort, which would be the more excellent?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam vasiṣṭhasya ca saṃvādaṃ brahmaṇaś ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recount this ancient tale, the dialogue of Vasiṣṭha and Brahmā, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: daivamānuṣayoḥ kiṃ svit karmaṇoḥ śreṣṭham ity uta purā vasiṣṭho bhagavān pitāmaham apṛcchata
english: "Of the two works, the divine and the human, which is the better?" — thus, of old, the venerable Vasiṣṭha questioned the Grandfather.

sanskrit: tataḥ padmodbhavo rājan devadevaḥ pitāmahaḥ uvāca madhuraṃ vākyam arthavad dhetubhūṣitam
english: Then, O king, the lotus-born Grandfather, god of gods, spoke a sweet utterance, weighty in meaning and adorned with reasons:

sanskrit: nābījaṃ jāyate kiṃ cin na bījena vinā phalam bījād bījaṃ prabhavati bījād eva phalaṃ smṛtam
english: "Nothing is born without a seed, nor is there fruit apart from the seed; from seed springs seed, and from seed alone, it is taught, comes fruit.

sanskrit: yādṛśaṃ vapate bījaṃ kṣetram āsādya karṣakaḥ sukṛte duṣkṛte vāpi tādṛśaṃ labhate phalam
english: Whatever seed the farmer sows when he comes upon a field, whether in good soil or bad, just such a fruit does he obtain.

sanskrit: yathā bījaṃ vinā kṣetram uptaṃ bhavati niṣphalam tathā puruṣakāreṇa vinā daivaṃ na sidhyati
english: As a field sown without seed proves fruitless, so without human effort fate does not bear fruit.

sanskrit: kṣetraṃ puruṣakāras tu daivaṃ bījam udāhṛtam kṣetrabījasamāyogāt tataḥ sasyaṃ samṛdhyate
english: Human effort is declared to be the field, and fate the seed; from the union of field and seed the crop thereby flourishes.

sanskrit: karmaṇaḥ phalanirvṛttiṃ svayam aśnāti kārakaḥ pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate loke kṛtasyāpy akṛtasya ca
english: The doer himself reaps the ripening fruit of his deed; this is plainly seen in the world, both of what is done and of what is left undone.

sanskrit: śubhena karmaṇā saukhyaṃ duḥkhaṃ pāpena karmaṇā kṛtaṃ sarvatra labhate nākṛtaṃ bhujyate kva cit
english: From a good deed comes happiness, from an evil deed sorrow; what is done is everywhere obtained, what is not done is nowhere enjoyed.

sanskrit: kṛtī sarvatra labhate pratiṣṭhāṃ bhāgyavikṣataḥ akṛtī labhate bhraṣṭaḥ kṣate kṣārāvasecanam
english: The man of action everywhere wins standing, even when fortune has wounded him; the idle and fallen man earns only a sprinkling of salt upon his wound.

sanskrit: tapasā rūpasaubhāgyaṃ ratnāni vividhāni ca prāpyate karmaṇā sarvaṃ na daivād akṛtātmanā
english: By austerity beauty and good fortune, and jewels of many kinds — all is gained by effort, not by fate, by one whose self is unprepared.

sanskrit: tathā svargaś ca bhogaś ca niṣṭhā yā ca manīṣitā sarvaṃ puruṣakāreṇa kṛtenehopapadyate
english: Likewise heaven, and enjoyment, and whatever consummation is desired — all this is attained here through human effort exerted.

sanskrit: jyotīṃṣi tridaśā nāgā yakṣāś candrārkamārutāḥ sarve puruṣakāreṇa mānuṣyād devatāṃ gatāḥ
english: The luminaries, the gods, the nāgas, the yakṣas, the moon, the sun, the winds — all, through human effort, have passed from the human state to godhood.

sanskrit: artho vā mitravargo vā aiśvaryaṃ vā kulānvitam śrīś cāpi durlabhā bhoktuṃ tathaivākṛtakarmabhiḥ
english: Wealth, or a circle of friends, or lordship attended by noble birth, and even prosperity — all are hard for the idle to come by and enjoy.

sanskrit: śaucena labhate vipraḥ kṣatriyo vikrameṇa ca vaiśyaḥ puruṣakāreṇa śūdraḥ śuśrūṣayā śriyam
english: By purity the brāhmaṇa wins prosperity, the kṣatriya by valor, the vaiśya by effort, and the śūdra by service.

sanskrit: nādātāraṃ bhajanty arthā na klībaṃ nāpi niṣkriyam nākarmaśīlaṃ nāśūraṃ tathā naivātapasvinam
english: Riches do not resort to the ungiving, nor to the impotent, nor to the inactive, nor to the slothful, nor to the cowardly, nor to one without austerity.

sanskrit: yena lokās trayaḥ sṛṣṭā daityāḥ sarvāś ca devatāḥ sa eṣa bhagavān viṣṇuḥ samudre tapyate tapaḥ
english: He by whom the three worlds were created, the daityas and all the gods — that very lord Viṣṇu performs austerity upon the ocean.

sanskrit: svaṃ cet karmaphalaṃ na syāt sarvam evāphalaṃ bhavet loko daivaṃ samālambya udāsīno bhaven na tu
english: If the fruit of one's own deed did not exist, all action would be fruitless; the world, leaning upon fate alone, would grow indifferent — but it is not so.

sanskrit: akṛtvā mānuṣaṃ karma yo daivam anuvartate vṛthā śrāmyati saṃprāpya patiṃ klībam ivāṅganā
english: He who, without doing the human work, follows after fate, toils in vain, like a woman who has gained an impotent husband.

sanskrit: na tathā mānuṣe loke bhayam asti śubhāśubhe yathā tridaśaloke hi bhayam alpena jāyate
english: There is not so much peril in the human world, in things good and ill, as there is in the world of the gods, where peril arises from a small cause.

sanskrit: kṛtaḥ puruṣakāras tu daivam evānuvartate na daivam akṛte kiṃ cit kasya cid dātum arhati
english: When human effort is made, fate follows after it; fate, where nothing is done, can give nothing to anyone.

sanskrit: yadā sthānāny anityāni dṛśyante daivateṣv api kathaṃ karma vinā daivaṃ sthāsyate sthāpayiṣyati
english: When even among the gods their stations are seen to be impermanent, how shall fate, without action, endure or make anything endure?

sanskrit: na daivatāni loke 'smin vyāpāraṃ yānti kasya cit vyāsaṅgaṃ janayanty ugram ātmābhibhavaśaṅkayā
english: The gods in this world do not engage in anyone's affairs; rather, fearing their own overthrow, they breed fierce contention.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca sadā bhavati vigrahaḥ kasya vācā hy adaivaṃ syād yato daivaṃ pravartate
english: Between the seers and the gods there is ever strife; for by whose word could there be a no-fate, since from these does fate proceed?

sanskrit: kathaṃ cāsya samutpattir yathā daivaṃ pravartate evaṃ tridaśaloke 'pi prāpyante bahavaś chalāḥ
english: And how does its origin come about, in the manner that fate sets in motion? Thus even in the world of the gods many deceptions are met with.

sanskrit: ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ ātmaiva cātmanaḥ sākṣī kṛtasyāpy akṛtasya ca
english: For the self alone is the friend of the self, the self alone the foe of the self; and the self alone is the witness of the self, of what is done and what is left undone.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ ca vikṛtaṃ kiṃ cit kṛte karmaṇi sidhyati sukṛte duṣkṛtaṃ karma na yathārthaṃ prapadyate
english: Something done and something marred alike comes to fruition when the deed is performed; but an evil deed laid upon a good one does not come duly to pass.

sanskrit: devānāṃ śaraṇaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvaṃ puṇyair avāpyate puṇyaśīlaṃ naraṃ prāpya kiṃ daivaṃ prakariṣyati
english: Merit is the refuge of the gods; all is won through meritorious acts. Against a man whose nature is meritorious, what will fate avail to do?

sanskrit: purā yayātir vibhraṣṭaś cyāvitaḥ patitaḥ kṣitau punar āropitaḥ svargaṃ dauhitraiḥ puṇyakarmabhiḥ
english: Of old Yayāti, undone, cast down, fallen to the earth, was raised again to heaven by his daughters' sons through their meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: purūravāś ca rājarṣir dvijair abhihitaḥ purā aila ity abhivikhyātaḥ svargaṃ prāpto mahīpatiḥ
english: And the royal sage Purūravas, addressed of old by the brāhmaṇas, renowned as Aila, that lord of the earth attained to heaven.

sanskrit: aśvamedhādibhir yajñaiḥ satkṛtaḥ kosalādhipaḥ maharṣiśāpāt saudāsaḥ puruṣādatvam āgataḥ
english: The lord of Kosala, honored by sacrifices such as the horse-sacrifice — Saudāsa, by the curse of a great seer, came to the state of a man-eater.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā ca rāmaś ca muniputrau dhanurdharau na gacchataḥ svargalokaṃ sukṛteneha karmaṇā
english: Aśvatthāman and Rāma, sons of sages and bearers of the bow, do not go to the world of heaven, even by their good deeds done here.

sanskrit: vasur yajñaśatair iṣṭvā dvitīya iva vāsavaḥ mithyābhidhānenaikena rasātalatalaṃ gataḥ
english: Vasu, having sacrificed with a hundred sacrifices, like a second Vāsava, by a single false utterance descended to the floor of the netherworld.

sanskrit: balir vairocanir baddho dharmapāśena daivataiḥ viṣṇoḥ puruṣakāreṇa pātālaśayanaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: Bali, son of Virocana, bound by the gods with the noose of dharma, was made to lie in Pātāla through the effort of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: śakrasyodasya caraṇaṃ prasthito janamejayaḥ dvijastrīṇāṃ vadhaṃ kṛtvā kiṃ daivena na vāritaḥ
english: Janamejaya, setting Śakra's foot aside, set forth — having wrought the slaying of brāhmaṇa women, why was he not restrained by fate?

sanskrit: ajñānād brāhmaṇaṃ hatvā spṛṣṭo bālavadhena ca vaiśaṃpāyanaviprarṣiḥ kiṃ daivena nivāritaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa sage Vaiśaṃpāyana, having unknowingly slain a brāhmaṇa and been touched by the killing of a child — why was he not held back by fate?

sanskrit: gopradānena mithyā ca brāhmaṇebhyo mahāmakhe purā nṛgaś ca rājarṣiḥ kṛkalāsatvam āgataḥ
english: And the royal sage Nṛga, of old, by a false gift of a cow to brāhmaṇas at a great sacrifice, came to the state of a lizard.
